verses.1: And Ben-Hadad, king of Aram, gathered all his army together. Thirty-two kings joined with him. He also had horses and chariots. He went up to Samaria and fought there.
verses.2: And he sent servants to Ahaziah, the king of Israel, with this message.
verses.3: And he said to him, “As it is written in the Book of Hades: ‘Your silver and gold shall be given to me. And your good children shall also be given to me.’”
verses.4: And the king of Israel said, “As you say, my Lord, the king, I and all who belong to me are yours.”
verses.5: And the magicians returned, and they said, “As it is written in the Book of Habakkuk: ‘I sent you to say, “Give me your gold, your silver, your treasures, and your children.”’”
verses.6: For if now, tomorrow, I send my servants to you, and they search for your house and the houses of your servants, then everything that is valuable in your sight will be given to them and taken away.
verses.7: And the king of Israel called out to all the elders of the land. He said, “Tell me, and see that this is indeed a bad thing. They have sent me to take away my women, children, livestock, and gold. I will not refuse them.”
verses.8: And they said to him, “All the elders and all the people, do not listen to him; do not follow his advice.”
verses.9: And he said to Malachai ben-Hadad, “Tell my lord, the king, that whatever you sent out your servant at first, I will do. But this cannot be done.” Then the magicians went away, and the matter remained unresolved.
verses.10: And He sent Bne-Hadad to him, and said, “Do this for me, O God. And let it be a sign that if Apar Shomron is thrown down, it will happen to all the people who are under my rule.”
verses.11: And the king of Israel said, “Let them speak. Do not be silent during the festival.”
verses.12: And when he heard this, he became furious. The kings also became angry. He said to his servants, “Attack the city!” And they did attack the city.
verses.13: And behold, a prophet came to Ahaz, the king of Israel. He said, “Thus says the LORD: ‘I have seen all this great disaster. Today, I will give it into your hands. Then you will know that I am the LORD.’”
verses.14: And Ahava said, “As the Lord has said to the sons of the kings of the nations: ‘Who can forbid war?’”
verses.15: And he punished the young men of the tribes of the nations. There were two thousand and thirty of them who were punished. After that, he punished all the people, all the children of Israel, in total seven thousand.
verses.16: And they went out at dawn. And Ben-Hadad broke down the gates of the city. And there were thirty-two kings who helped him.
verses.17: And the young men of the tribes of the nations went out first. They sent one of them and told him, “People have come out from Shomron.”
verses.18: And he said, “If they go out to make peace, then they will be saved. But if they go out to fight, then they will be destroyed.”
verses.19: And these were the men who came out of the city: the young men of the tribes and the army that followed them.
verses.20: And each man attacked his enemy. Israel pursued them. The king of Aram was defeated by Israel. He was captured on a horse and with his troops.
verses.21: And the king of Israel went out, mounted his horse, and rode in his chariot. He attacked the Ammonites with great force.
verses.22: The prophet went to the king of Israel and said to him, “Be strong. Know that when the year comes again, the king of Aram will attack you.”
verses.23: And the servants of King Aram said to him, “The gods of the mountains are our gods. Therefore, they will strengthen us over us. But if we do not strengthen ourselves against them, then we must fight against them in battle.”
verses.24: And this was done by the princes, one by one from their positions, and they placed bags under them.
verses.25: And you shall have sheep like those that fall from your flock, and horses like those that run away from your stable. You shall fight against them in the field, if you do not strengthen yourselves against them. Then he will hear their cries and act accordingly.
verses.26: And when the year came to an end, Ben-Hadad attacked Syria. He went up against Israel in battle.
verses.27: And the children of Israel gathered together and went out to battle. They camped opposite two enemy armies: the Amorites and the Canaanites. The land was filled with fear and chaos.
verses.28: And the man of God went and said to the king of Israel, “As the LORD has said, ‘Aram is the god of the mountains; Jehovah is not the god of the valleys.’ I have given you all this great power in your hands. Now know that I am the LORD.”
verses.29: And they camped there for seven days. On the seventh day, war broke out. And the children of Israel attacked the Amorites over a distance of a hundred thousand cubits in one day.
verses.30: And the fugitives rushed towards the city. The heat pressed down upon them; there were twenty-seven thousand fugitives. And Ben-Hadad also came into the city through a hole in the wall.
verses.31: And his servants said to him, “Please hear this: We have heard that the kings of Israel are kings of kindness. Please accept our gifts and gifts from our people. Then we will go before the king of Israel, so that your life may be saved.”
verses.32: They put on their armor and weapons on their heads. Then they went before the king of Israel. They said, “Your servant, son of David, please save my life.” The king replied, “Live on, my brother!”
verses.33: And the men guessed what had happened. They rushed forward and decided to go after him. They said, “Your brother, son of Haddad!” Then they went to find him. They brought him onto the chariot.
verses.34: And he said to him, “The towns that my father took from your father, I will return them to you. And the lands will be given to you as a gift, just as my father gave them to Shemeron. I will make a covenant with you, and I will send him away.” He made a covenant with him, and then sent him away.
verses.35: And one of the prophets said to his companion, “Speak to me about what God has commanded.” So the man obeyed and spoke accordingly.
verses.36: And he said to him, “Because you did not hear the voice of the LORD, you will go away from me. And so, the lion went away from him. Then the lion found him and killed him.”
verses.37: And another man found him. He said, “Please cut it down.” So the man cut it down and wounded it.
verses.38: And the prophet went and stood before the king on the road. He searched for the place where the treasure was hidden, with his eyes wide open.
verses.39: And the king went ahead, and he cried out to the king. He said, “Your servant has gone into the battlefield. Now, there’s a man who comes to me. Tell him to keep this man safe. If he gets captured, your life will be at risk, or you will be forced to pay him in gold.”
verses.40: And your servant continued to do this day after day. But he wasn’t the one who deserved to be punished. So I said to him, “King of Israel, this is your judgment. You have indeed done wrong.”
verses.41: And he rushed away, putting aside the apheresis from his eyes. He became king of Israel, because he was one of the prophets.
verses.42: And He said to him, “As Jehovah has said, you have sent out a man from Karmi. Now your soul will be under his control, and your people will be under his control as well.”
verses.43: And he went through Israel, traveling along their homes, filled with anger and indignation. Then he arrived in Shomron.
